Update 2026-07-17 (auto-dev, 1am session): Built the natural follow-up flagged last session — clip playback was completely missing, so the detected hit chips led nowhere. Root cause: ClipRecorder's onUploaded callback discarded the uploaded clip URL (only awarded credits) and the detected shuttle-hit timestamps never left component state — neither made it into the saved match record. Fixed the whole pipe: LiveMatchModal now captures both into its live-match state, handleLogMatch carries clipUrl/shuttleHits onto the logged Match, and they persist through the existing live_stats jsonb side-channel (same pattern as pointLog/liveStats — no schema change). MatchDetailModal now renders the clip as a <video> with tap-to-seek chips for each detected hit. npx next build clean, deployed (commit 1e0f5bb). Still needs Lok: real match test to confirm playback + seeking works with an actual recorded clip (no camera/video in this environment).

most device-feasible, no cloud cost, fits the static-export/no-backend constraint). Shipped: src/lib/shuttleDetect.ts — decodes the clip's existing audio track (mic was already being recorded for every clip) via the Web Audio API, detects "thwock" transients as energy spikes above a rolling local mean+stddev threshold with a 300ms refractory period so one hit isn't double-counted. Runs automatically once after recording stops in ClipRecorder (both camera and iOS native-file-input paths) — no toggle needed, it's read-only analysis with zero live performance cost. Detected hit timestamps show as a chip list (mm:ss) on the "Recording complete" screen. Self-check src/lib/shuttleDetect.selfcheck.ts passes (synthetic energy spikes: correct timestamps, refractory collapsing, silence produces zero false hits). npx next build clean, deployed.
Caveat: there's no clip playback/scrubbing screen anywhere in the app yet
